Priya M.: RFC follow-up: proposing hybrid fallback - local fast coordinator + optional central arbitrator. Goal: keep tail latency low but keep global safety.
Alex B.: what failure modes?
Priya M.: model regressions, sudden node OOMs, regional partitions, and slow control-plane telemetry.
Samir K.: local autonomy helps on partitions but we risk state drift. How do we reconcile?
Priya M.: nodes emit compact action logs with per-node seq nums. Central uses LWW with generation counters and can issue higher-precedence directives.
Elena R.: local policy must be tiny: thresholds + cooldowns (default cooldown 2m). Also require a compatibility blob cached on node (TTL 5m).
Alex B.: private/VPC installs?
Priya M.: support autonomous-only mode: local logs persisted and shipped on reconnect. Central ingests with rate-limits and dedupe by node+seq.
Samir K.: replay storms on reconnect need caps and replay pacing. Central should ack ranges and reject duplicates.
Elena R.: add cost_delta in action events for cost/observability. Also alert if central and node disagree >10m.
Priya M.: open items: action-log schema (compact vs verbose), reconciliation alg (LWW vs merge), and sane defaults. Samir will draft reconciliation blurb; Alex will mock control-plane directive POST /v1/directives.
deploy-bot: "deployment: canary-hybrid 0.2.0 -> staging succeeded" :white_check_mark:
Priya M.: I'll update RFC with hybrid flow, policy snippet and runbook tomorrow. Tagging @Samir K., @Alex B., @Elena R.
